q: Which statement about paediatric renal imaging is FALSE?
o: Fetal urine enters amniotic fluid after 10 weeks
US is insensitive for detecting VUR
e: Hydronephrosis is not always obstruction. Amniotic fluid contains no fetal urine before 10 weeks. Ultrasound is not sensitive for VUR. Hypoechoic infant pyramids with a sharp corticomedullary junction can be mistaken for hydronephrosis. US is the first test for suspected obstruction and for follow-up; VCUG or diuresis renography follow as indicated.
b: No fetal urine in amniotic fluid before 10 weeks

q: The FDA warning on anaesthesia and brain development applies to repeated or lengthy exposure in:
e: Families should be told what is known and which studies are under way. Update: the GAS trial (2019) and PANDA showed no neurodevelopmental harm from a single short anaesthetic in infancy. Anaesthesia risks include nausea, vomiting, bronchospasm, laryngospasm, stridor, emergence delirium and maladaptive behaviour.
b: FDA: repeated/long anaesthesia <3 years or 3rd trimester
GAS trial: single short GA in infancy safe

q: During orchidopexy, a boy has an absent vas deferens and a 3-mm golden-yellow nodule on the cord. What should be checked next?
e: The nodule is ectopic adrenal cortex (no medulla); the adrenal forms just medial to the gonadal ridge, so rests occur along the cord. The vas and ureteric bud both come from the wolffian duct: 79% of men with an absent vas lack the ipsilateral kidney.
b: Yellow cord nodule = adrenal rest (cortex only)
79% with absent vas lack that kidney

q: Which statement about penile carcinoma in situ (Tis) is FALSE?
o: Topical imiquimod or 5-FU can treat it
Bowenoid papulosis is a form of penile Tis
Erythroplasia of Queyrat involves the shaft skin
Bowen disease involves shaft, genital or perineal skin
e: Location defines the names: erythroplasia of Queyrat on the glans or prepuce, Bowen disease on the shaft, genitalia or perineum. Tis has three clinical forms: Bowenoid papulosis, Bowen disease, erythroplasia of Queyrat. Small noninvasive lesions: local excision, circumcision (preputial), fulguration (recurs), 5% 5-FU or imiquimod, Nd:YAG laser.
b: Tis forms: Bowenoid papulosis, Bowen, Queyrat

q: Which condition does NOT warrant 24-hour urine metabolic testing after a first stone?
e: No direct link exists between neurological disorders and stones. Risk factors warranting testing include hyperparathyroidism, obesity, bowel disease or bypass, gout, diabetes and recurrent stones. First-time formers have a 50% recurrence risk; men have higher incidence and recurrence. Obesity increases stone risk.
s: Ch 92 Stone evaluation and medical management
b: Test if hyperparathyroid, obese, bowel disease, bypass
First stone: 50% recur; men recur more

q: Which statement about congenital bladder diverticula is FALSE?
o: They are usually solitary and large
They lie lateral to the ureteric orifice
e: Congenital diverticula are solitary, often large, in smooth-walled bladders without outlet obstruction, usually lateral and posterior to the ureteric orifice and often with VUR. Dome diverticula may relate to prune belly, valves or urachal anomalies. A Hutch diverticulum encompasses the orifice in a neurogenic bladder with reflux. Congenital diverticula are not associated with malignancy.
b: Lateral/posterior to orifice, often with VUR; Hutch if neurogenic

q: Which combination best predicts pathologic stage in prostate cancer?
e: Each predicts stage, but combined (with extent of cancer on biopsy) accuracy improves. PSA >8 ng/mL contributes significantly to biochemical recurrence risk. At least 10% of new cases are locally advanced. Nomograms tend to overestimate recurrence risk in high-risk men.
b: Combine PSA, grade, clinical stage (+ biopsy extent)
Nomograms overestimate risk in high-risk men

q: Which is NOT one of the four key elements of a successful diuresis renogram?
e: Key elements: hydration, region of interest, bladder drainage as appropriate, diuretic timing. Review all parameters, because technique variations skew results.

q: According to the book, which fasting time before anaesthesia in children is correct?
e: Book (ASA-based): clear fluids 2 h, breast milk 4 h, formula, nonhuman milk or light meal 6 h, full meal 8 h. Enteral feeds count as a fatty meal (stop 8 h). NPO violation increases aspiration and pneumonitis. Update: several European societies now allow clear fluids up to 1 h before induction in children.
b: Formula, nonhuman milk, light meal 6 h
Full or fatty meal (and enteral feeds) 8 h

q: A girl with right renal agenesis has cyclic abdominal pain and a pelvic mass after menarche. The likely associated anomaly is:
o: An imperforate hymen on its own
A large anterior Gartner duct cyst
e: OHVIRA (obstructed hemivagina, ipsilateral renal agenesis; Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich): an insult early in week 4 affecting wolffian duct and ureteric bud gives a didelphic uterus with obstructed horn and vagina. Before week 4: renal agenesis with a unicornuate uterus. Female reproductive anomalies are common with unilateral agenesis; commonest müllerian anomaly is a true unicornuate uterus or a bicornuate uterus with rudimentary horn.

q: Which statement about the aetiology of penile cancer is FALSE?
o: Gonorrhoea is not a proven risk factor
HPV is a recognised aetiological agent
Lichen sclerosus is a risk factor
e: Circumcision after 21 offers little protection; neonatal circumcision protects. Risk factors: no neonatal circumcision, phimosis, HPV, tobacco, lichen sclerosus, perhaps trauma; no link with gonorrhoea, syphilis, herpes, occupation, marijuana or alcohol. HPV in men is linked to partners' cervical dysplasia and cancer. Largely preventable (neonatal circumcision, HPV vaccination, behaviour). Rare in developed countries; US data show disparity for Puerto Rican Hispanic men. Lichen sclerosus (BXO) has no known viral cause.
b: HPV is causal (also partners' cervical cancer)
Risks: phimosis, LS, tobacco, no neonatal circumcision
No link with gonorrhoea, syphilis, alcohol

q: Which is NOT routinely measured in a stone-risk 24-hour urine collection?
e: AUA (Pearle 2014): one or two 24-h collections on a random diet for volume, pH, calcium, oxalate, uric acid, citrate, sodium, potassium and creatinine. Sulfate reflects protein intake. Completeness: creatinine about 1 mg/kg/h (20–25 mg/kg/day in men).
s: Ch 92 Stone evaluation and medical management
b: Volume, pH, Ca, oxalate, urate, citrate, Na, K, creatinine

q: Which statement about acquired bladder diverticula is FALSE?
o: Their wall lacks a proper muscularis propria
They often lie near the ureteric orifice
They are commoner in women than men
e: Acquired diverticula are commoner in men; ~70% have outlet obstruction (in men prostatic; in women iatrogenic, dysfunctional, neurogenic or masses) or neurogenic dysfunction. They lie near the orifice (relative weakness) and may adhere to the ureter, affecting surgery. The hallmark is an incomplete, disorganised muscularis propria; no trabeculation in the wall.
b: Near ureteric orifice; adherent to ureter

q: Neoadjuvant ADT before radical prostatectomy has been shown to:
e: Margins fall in cT1–T2 but not cT3c, and long-term PSA-free survival does not improve, so it has no role. Clinical overstaging occurs in about 27% of cT3 men (range 7–26%). PSA recurrence after RP depends on Gleason score, ECE, SVI, nodes and margins.

q: Which statement about sonographic renal patterns in children is FALSE?
o: MCDK has random cysts of varying size
A renal mass on US should be followed by CT
e: ARPKD: bilateral enlarged echogenic kidneys. MCDK: randomly distributed cysts of varying size with scant hyperechoic parenchyma. ADPKD: bilateral, parenchyma replaced by cysts. Age and US features suggest a mass's nature, but contrast CT should follow.
b: MCDK: random cysts, little hyperechoic parenchyma
Renal mass: follow with contrast CT

q: Which statement about perioperative care of premature infants is FALSE?
o: Target oxygen saturation is close to 100%
They are at high risk of apnoea
Skin evaporation causes large fluid losses
e: Supplemental oxygen risks retinopathy and blindness, so aim for saturation in the low 90s. Premature infants: high risk of apnoea (can be fatal), more perioperative complications, large evaporative losses, poor concentrating ability. Surfactant deficiency (<36 weeks) means high oxygen consumption, low FRC and tracheomalacia.

q: Which statement about horseshoe kidney is FALSE?
o: It raises renal cell carcinoma risk
It is associated with Turner syndrome
It is the commonest fusion anomaly
Its isthmus usually lies at L3–L4
e: Horseshoe kidney is the commonest fusion anomaly; the isthmus lies at L3–L4, is bulky parenchyma with its own blood supply; supply is variable. UPJ obstruction in one-third. Wilms tumour and renal pelvic tumours are commoner, but not RCC. Turner syndrome (45,X): horseshoe kidney and coarctation, so karyotype (also lymphoedema, shield chest, low hairline, webbed neck).
b: No increased RCC risk; Wilms and pelvic tumours up
Isthmus at L3–L4, own blood supply

q: Which statement about presentation of penile cancer is FALSE?
o: Hypercalcaemia may be PTH-like and paraneoplastic
Pain brings most patients within a month
It occurs most often on the glans (48%)
15–50% delay care for over a year
e: Patients with penile cancer delay more than most: 15–50% wait over a year; delay in biopsy is also common. Sites: glans 48%, prepuce 21%; it starts on the glans or prepuce and enlarges. Hypercalcaemia may come from PTH-like substances activating osteoclasts. Distant metastases occur late.

q: A man's 24-h urine shows creatinine of 50 mg/kg and high calcium, oxalate, sodium and urate. The most likely explanation is:
e: Normal male creatinine is 20–25 mg/kg/day; a value near 50 suggests a 48-h collection, making all values unreliable.
s: Ch 92 Stone evaluation and medical management

q: Which statement about tumours in bladder diverticula is FALSE?
o: The whole lining must be inspected
A small papillary lesion should be biopsied
Deep biopsy is safe for staging
e: With no muscle wall, deep biopsy risks perforation (and dissemination), yet without it staging is hard. Urothelial cancer is commonest. Biopsy any papillary lesion carefully (a 3-mm lesion can be biopsied without a resectoscope). Inspect the entire interior; image upper tracts; retrograde pyelograms only if indicated. A well-draining asymptomatic diverticulum still needs annual cystoscopy and cytology (natural history unknown, stasis may promote cancer).
b: Annual cystoscopy and cytology; inspect whole lining

q: Which statement about high-dose bicalutamide (150 mg) is FALSE?
o: It improves survival in localised disease
It reduces progression in locally advanced disease
It may help survival in advanced disease
e: In localised disease it increased the risk of death (HR 1.23). Early ADT may benefit aggressive subsets at the cost of side effects.
b: 43% less progression in locally advanced disease
Early ADT may help aggressive subsets

q: Which statement about imaging after febrile UTI in children is FALSE?
o: A normal US excludes significant VUR
e: US is used first despite low yield; a normal sonogram does not risk-stratify or predict VUR. Bottom-up: US then VCUG finds all VUR (may overtreat low grades). Top-down: DMSA for pyelonephritis/scarring; VCUG only if DMSA abnormal. (AAP 2011: US after first febrile UTI; VCUG if US abnormal or recurrent UTI.)
b: Normal US does not exclude VUR
Top-down: DMSA first, VCUG if abnormal
AAP 2011: US after first febrile UTI

q: Which statement about preoperative medical preparation in children is FALSE (per the book)?
o: Give antiseizure and asthma drugs on the morning
e: Book: fasting with stopped diabetic medicines causes volume depletion and hyperglycaemia (the 'hypoglycaemia' version is the false statement). Ketogenic diet: carbohydrate-free fluids. Metformin stopped 24 h before (lactic acidosis risk with dehydration or hypoxaemia). Give antiseizure, reflux and asthma medicines on the morning. Labs: opening the urinary tract is clean-contaminated; routine tests are not cost-effective; pregnancy test for females of childbearing age; routine chest x-ray is not recommended.

q: Which statement about renal ectopia is FALSE?
o: Solitary ectopia has the most associated anomalies
Ectopic kidneys show no sex predilection
e: Most are asymptomatic, except those with an ectopic ureter. The pelvis lies anterior (incomplete rotation); 56% hydronephrotic: half obstruction (70% UPJ, 30% UVJ), 25% reflux ≥grade 3, 25% malrotation. Solitary ectopia has the most anomalies (cryptorchidism; vaginal atresia, uterine anomalies). Genital anomalies are associated. In crossed fusion the upper pole of the ectopic kidney joins the lower pole of the normal one; ureters are orthotopic. Normal rotation is 90° medially between weeks 6 and 9. Sex: bilateral agenesis ~75% male; unilateral 1.8:1; crossed fused 3:2; simple ectopia equal.

q: Which statement about penile cancer histology and staging is FALSE?
o: SCC subtypes split by HPV relationship
Cavernosal invasion is T2 in TNM 8
Stage, grade and LVI predict metastasis
e: TNM 8: T2 invades corpus spongiosum; T3 invades corpus cavernosum (worse prognosis). Most are squamous cell carcinoma with keratin pearls; subtypes are divided into HPV-related and non-HPV groups. Stage, grade, vascular and perineural invasion predict metastasis. Biopsy (frozen section can precede definitive surgery) is essential. TNM 8 includes clinical and pathological descriptors.
b: Stage, grade, LVI, PNI predict nodes

q: Which statement about enteric hyperoxaluria is FALSE?
o: It mainly causes calcium oxalate stones
Fat malabsorption frees oxalate for absorption
Oxalate is absorbed mainly in the small bowel
e: Oxalate is absorbed mainly in the colon; bile salts and fatty acids increase colonic permeability, and fat binds calcium as soaps, leaving free oxalate. Calcium oxalate stones form from hyperoxaluria, hypocitraturia (bicarbonate loss, hypokalaemia; acid-base status is the main regulator of citrate), hypomagnesuria and low volume. Treat with fluids, potassium citrate and calcium supplements (calcium citrate ideal) to bind oxalate. Roux-en-Y bypass causes hyperoxaluria, low volume and hypocitraturia; band or sleeve mainly low volume.
s: Ch 92 Stone evaluation and medical management
b: Treat: fluids, K citrate, calcium supplements

q: An anticoagulated man with recurrent UTI, a large diverticulum and low detrusor pressure is best managed by:
e: Major surgery is high risk; TURP is risky on anticoagulants and will not empty a diverticulum with low detrusor pressure; recurrent UTI makes observation poor. Diverticula are usually incidental; no specific symptoms; may cause UTI and pyuria. Complications: UTI, stones, carcinoma, upper tract deterioration. Saccules and cellules accompany obstruction; reflux uncommon except Hutch; large diverticula may deviate the pelvic ureter medially.
b: TURP won't empty a low-pressure diverticulum
Recurrent UTI: do not just observe

q: For locally advanced prostate cancer treated with radiotherapy, trials (RTOG, EORTC) support:
e: Longer ADT with EBRT improves outcomes in high-grade disease. Doses ≥78 Gy improve primary RT outcomes; adjuvant RT doses >60 Gy (threshold ~61.2–64 Gy). Long ADT (>6–9 months) with RT may increase rectal morbidity and sexual dysfunction. CaPSURE shows more RP and less primary ADT and RT for high-risk disease.
b: Primary RT ≥78 Gy; adjuvant RT >60 Gy
Long ADT: more rectal and sexual toxicity
CaPSURE: more RP, less primary ADT

q: Which statement about trauma and scrotal imaging in children is FALSE?
o: Delayed CT views complete trauma imaging
US is reliable for impalpable testes
e: US is unreliable for the undescended testis (except perhaps inguinal testis in an overweight boy). US compares favourably with CT in acute trauma and follows haematomas or urinomas; CT uses ionising radiation and contrast; delayed parenchymal/collecting views or lateral cystourethral views complete it. Scrotal US with history and exam separates inflammation, tumour, trauma and torsion; scintigraphy adds little. Torsion of the appendix testis is NOT an enlarged avascular lower-pole nodule with hyperaemia (book).
b: Delayed CT views complete trauma study

q: Which statement about children with spina bifida and other conditions is FALSE?
o: Spina bifida raises latex allergy risk
e: Autonomic dysreflexia (lesions T5–T8 or above) causes uncontrolled hypertension, bradycardia, stroke, even death; know its signs. Spina bifida has many comorbidities and latex allergy risk; latex anaphylaxis: bronchoconstriction, vasodilation, hypotension, capillary leak, coronary spasm. CAH: epinephrine and cortisol deficiency, hypoglycaemia. CKD 2: no drug adjustment but watch NSAIDs. Sickle cell: avoid dehydration during fasting. Bleomycin plus high inspired oxygen: fatal pulmonary toxicity.

q: Which statement about unilateral renal agenesis is FALSE?
o: The ipsilateral ureter is absent in 60%
e: Adrenal agenesis occurs in <10%; the adrenal is usually normally placed (maybe flattened). Incidence 1:1100. Ipsilateral ureter absent in 60%; contralateral ureter anomalies common; 25% of contralateral ureters reflux. Gonads normal; epididymal head forms (mesonephric tubules). Splenic flexure gas in the left renal fossa suggests left agenesis or ectopia. Diagnose with US, DMSA or MRA. Solitary kidney: annual BP and urine protein checks (CKD risk); VCUG not mandatory.
b: Contralateral VUR 25%; annual BP and proteinuria

q: Which statement about staging the penile primary is FALSE?
o: US and MRI cannot detect cavernosal invasion
Physical exam best stages small distal lesions
Artificial erection MRI helps when exam is unclear
e: US had 100% sensitivity for cavernosal invasion in one study; US and contrast MRI both help before organ-sparing surgery. Examination is most reliable for small distal lesions; examine both primary and groins.
b: Exam best for small distal lesions
Artificial erection MRI if exam unclear

q: Which statement about uric acid stones is FALSE?
o: Solubility at pH 7 is 10× that at pH 5
Low urine pH is the key determinant
Allopurinol is first line for most
Target urine pH is about 6.0 to 6.5
e: Low pH (below the pKa 5.5, often ~5) drives crystallisation more than volume or hyperuricosuria. Potassium citrate to pH 6.0–6.5 is key; allopurinol mainly if urinary uric acid >1500 mg/day. Solubility >10× higher at pH 7 than 5, so measured uric acid rises after alkalinisation. Over-alkalinisation (>7) causes calcium phosphate stones (keep 6.5–7.0 in gouty diathesis). Lesch-Nyhan causes uric acid stones; hyperuricosuria also promotes calcium oxalate stones (heterogeneous nucleation). Diabetes gives acidic urine (uric acid, calcium oxalate stones).
s: Ch 92 Stone evaluation and medical management

q: Female urethral diverticula most often arise from:
e: Recurrent infection of periurethral glands, obstruction, suburethral abscess and rupture into the urethra. They lie within the urethropelvic ligament between endopelvic and periurethral fascia. Ostia: middle/distal third at 4 and 8 o'clock (ventrolateral), best seen at cystoscopy, too small for US. They can be partial, anterior or circumferential.
b: May be partial, anterior or circumferential

q: Which statement about adjuvant RT after radical prostatectomy is FALSE?
o: SV invasion predicts progression despite RT
e: SWOG 8794 and EORTC 22911 showed better biochemical, metastasis-free and overall survival (SWOG) and local control for pT3; margin-positive men benefit most. Book: the role remains controversial and benefiting subsets are ill defined. SV or node involvement predicts progression despite local therapy. N+ after RP: ECOG 3886 (immediate ADT improved survival); ADT plus RT may be better; no proven role for adjuvant chemotherapy. Update: RADICALS-RT, RAVES and GETUG-AFU 17 favour early salvage over routine adjuvant RT.
b: SVI or N+ progress despite local therapy

q: Per the book, which step is part of the response to suspected malignant hyperthermia?
o: Give more volatile agent to deepen anaesthesia
Give succinylcholine to relax rigid muscles
Stop trigger, call help, art line, Foley
Cool slowly and wait for laboratory results
e: Book answer: stop the trigger, call for help, change the machine, place arterial line and catheter. Corrections to the book's distractors: MH is rare; triggered by volatile agents and succinylcholine; early signs hypercarbia, tachycardia, masseter spasm, hyperthermia; late signs metabolic acidosis, hyperkalaemia, rigidity, rhabdomyolysis. Dantrolene is the specific treatment.
b: Stop trigger, call help, change machine

q: Which statement about renal vascular anomalies is FALSE?
o: Most renal AV fistulas are congenital
The apical segmental artery varies most
e: Fewer than 25% of renal AVFs are congenital (cirsoid, multiple communications, present in 3rd–4th decade, women 3:1, upper pole 45%); they cause renin-mediated hypertension in 50%. Renal arteries are end arteries without collaterals. The apical segmental artery varies most in origin (anterior division 43%). Megacalycosis: nonobstructive dilated, sometimes more numerous calyces; male 6:1. Infundibulopelvic stenosis is usually bilateral with VUR.

q: Which statement about inguinal metastases in penile cancer is FALSE?
o: A node over 4 cm suggests extranodal spread
Nodal extent is the main survival factor
Pelvic nodes are not first-echelon nodes
Nodes drain first to deep inguinal nodes
e: Preputial and shaft lymphatics drain to superficial inguinal nodes (outside the fascia lata) by embolisation. Presence and extent of inguinal metastasis is the most important prognostic factor. Good surgical outcome (>70% 5-year): ≤2 nodes, unilateral, no ENE, no pelvic nodes; nodes >4 cm often have ENE. Examination is the gold standard in nonobese men; CT/MRI for obese or previously operated groins; CT in node-positive men to find poor-prognosis features; PET/CT for pelvic/distant disease. Persistent palpable nodes: US- or CT-guided biopsy. Record clinical and pathological node factors.
b: Good prognosis: ≤2 nodes, unilateral, no ENE, no pelvic

q: Which statement about struvite stones is FALSE?
o: E. coli is a typical urease producer
They may harbour large amounts of endotoxin
Recurrent UTI is a key risk factor
e: E. coli usually lacks urease. Urea-splitters (Proteus) make ammonia; with matrix, carbonate apatite and bacteria, magnesium ammonium phosphate forms rapidly into staghorns; trapped bacteria perpetuate infection; stones may carry endotoxin. Recurrent UTI and anatomic abnormalities are risks; metabolic disorders coexist, especially in mixed stones, so do a metabolic evaluation. Acetohydroxamic acid 250 mg tds inhibits urease and can dissolve small stones; up to 30% get minor side effects, 15% DVT on long-term use.
s: Ch 92 Stone evaluation and medical management
b: Recurrent UTI; check metabolic causes too

q: Which is NOT a recognised feature of female urethral diverticulum?
e: The '3 Ds' (dysuria, post-void dribbling, dyspareunia) are rarely all present; some are asymptomatic. Size does not predict symptoms, cancer or infection, but large saddlebag diverticula recur more. A Skene gland abscess distorts the meatus; Skene glands do not communicate with the urethra. Gartner duct cysts lie on the anterolateral vaginal wall from cervix to introitus. Urethral mucosal prolapse occurs in prepubertal girls and postmenopausal women.

q: After RP, a man with rising PSA has a soft-tissue mass anterior to the rectum at the vesicourethral anastomosis on CT. Most likely:
e: Its position anterior to the rectum at the anastomosis argues against a node or seminal vesicle remnant.
b: Mass at anastomosis, anterior to rectum

q: Which statement about pain in children is FALSE?
o: Self-reported pain scales work under age 2
e: Self-assessment pain scales are not usable under 2 years. Discussing expectations and using child life specialists lowers anxiety; preoperative anxiety predicts postoperative pain and emergence delirium. Discuss pain with anaesthesia; use multimodal analgesia; dispose of unused narcotics properly. Most cardiac events are preventable; complications occur mostly early postoperatively.
b: Anxiety predicts postoperative pain and delirium

q: Which statement about bilateral renal agenesis is FALSE?
o: Parents and siblings should have renal US
Potter facies and lung hypoplasia occur
The adrenal glands are usually absent
e: Adrenals are usually normally placed; ureters almost always absent; bladder absent or hypoplastic; 40% stillborn; oligohydramnios, Potter facies, pulmonary hypoplasia. Screen parents and siblings with US. Maternal diabetes triples risk of agenesis and dysplasia. Survivors with agenesis may have reduced renal reserve and ESRD risk.
b: Screen parents and siblings; maternal diabetes ×3

q: Which statement about staging the groin in clinically node-negative penile cancer is FALSE?
o: Laparoscopic or robotic ILND gives similar yields
Anatomic sentinel node biopsy is recommended
Dynamic sentinel node biopsy suits expert centres
e: Fixed-site (anatomic) sentinel biopsy is unreliable and no longer recommended. Options for cN0 with adverse primary features: dynamic sentinel node biopsy (low morbidity, validated at high-volume centres), superficial ILND (reliable but morbid), modified complete dissection, laparoscopic/robotic ILND (comparable yields; more data needed for cN+). Low-risk (Tis, verrucous): little metastatic risk. Bilateral staging is supported (bilateral drainage; contralateral metastases in >50% in some series). Morbidity is falling.

q: Which statement about cystinuria is FALSE?
o: Cystine is 200× more soluble than cysteine
Tiopronin is as effective as penicillamine
e: Thiols cleave cystine into cysteine, which is about 200 times more soluble. Autosomal recessive defect of cystine, ornithine, lysine, arginine transport; homozygotes supersaturate; onset in the 1st–2nd decade; family history uncommon. Aim for concentration below 200–250 mg/L, so combine drugs with high urine output. α-MPG (tiopronin) equals D-penicillamine with less toxicity; no need to switch a stable patient. Children with stones need full work-up (cystinuria, RTA, primary hyperoxaluria); consider furosemide in neonates. Indinavir stones may be invisible on CT.
s: Ch 92 Stone evaluation and medical management
b: Cysteine is 200× more soluble than cystine

q: Which statement about urethral diverticulectomy is FALSE?
o: Use an autologous sling for coexisting SUI
e: Preserve the distinct periurethral fascial layer for reconstruction and to prevent fistula. Remove the sac and ostium (catheter seen through the defect) and close primarily with absorbable suture; flaps are not required. Synthetic slings risk erosion, so use autologous fascia. Complications: fistula, de novo SUI (~10%), injury to urethra, bladder, ureters with large diverticula. VCUG without post-void films may miss it; MRI (or US, CT, double-balloon) can show saddlebag diverticula. Adenocarcinoma is the commonest malignancy in urethral diverticula.
b: Autologous sling if SUI; de novo SUI ~10%

q: Which statement about perioperative infection in children is FALSE?
o: Bacterial UTI is the commonest fever cause
Transfusion can cause fever for a week
Give antibiotics as soon as sepsis is suspected
Recurrent preoperative UTI raises infection risk
e: The commonest infectious cause of perioperative fever is a viral upper respiratory infection; respiratory infection causes airway hyperreactivity for 2–8 weeks. Transfusion can cause fever up to a week. Obtain and treat urine cultures preoperatively when indicated; recurrent UTI raises risk. Antibiotics are the mainstay of sepsis and of surgical site infection prevention (timed for tissue levels at incision). Trauma: assume a full stomach (rapid sequence induction); nerve blocks help septic children. Anaphylaxis: NMBAs and β-lactams; stop drug, 100% oxygen, Trendelenburg, fluids, epinephrine. ERAS is not yet established in children.

q: Which is NOT an indication to repair a renal artery aneurysm (per the book)?
e: Book indications: uncontrolled hypertension, incomplete ring calcification, size >2.5 cm, woman of childbearing age or pregnant, growth, associated AVF, rupture, distal emboli. Update: SVS 2020 suggests repair for >3 cm in good-risk patients, and any size in women who may become pregnant.

q: Which statement about penile-preserving treatment is FALSE?
o: Local recurrence is lower than amputation
Mohs surgery and laser are options
RT suits T1–T2 tumours under 4 cm
e: Local recurrence is higher with organ preservation, but detected and treated recurrence does not reduce early survival. Ideal: Tis, Ta, T1, grade 1–2; aim to keep glans sensation or penile length. Options: limited excision, Mohs, laser; amputation for large or deeply invasive lesions. RT (EBRT or brachytherapy) for T1–T2 <4 cm; also for those refusing surgery or for palliation; nodal staging criteria are the same. 20% of recurrences occur after 5 years; salvage penectomy can cure.

q: Which statement about renal hypercalciuria is FALSE?
o: Its primary defect is tubular calcium leak
Calcium restriction does not help it
e: Renal leak lowers serum calcium, raising PTH and 1,25-vitamin D, which increase bone resorption and gut absorption; serum calcium is normal (unlike primary hyperparathyroidism); radial bone density low or low-normal. Calcium restriction has no effect. Hypercalciuria without hypercalcaemia: absorptive, renal leak, or normocalcaemic hyperparathyroidism. Moderate calcium with low sodium and less animal protein cuts calcium stone episodes ~50% (protein raises calcium, oxalate, uric acid).
s: Ch 92 Stone evaluation and medical management

q: Which statement about thiazides in hypercalciuria is FALSE?
o: Potassium citrate is the preferred supplement
High dietary sodium boosts their effect
e: Sodium increases urinary calcium and blocks the hypocalciuric action of thiazides, so restrict sodium. Thiazides increase distal tubular calcium reabsorption and, via volume depletion, proximal reabsorption. Side effects: hypokalaemia (cramps, weakness), hypocitraturia (from intracellular acidosis), low magnesium, glucose intolerance, hyperuricaemia, sexual dysfunction; check electrolytes 1–2 weeks after starting; add potassium citrate. They may unmask hyperparathyroidism. Update: NOCHOL trial (2023): hydrochlorothiazide did not reduce stone recurrence.
s: Ch 92 Stone evaluation and medical management
b: Add potassium citrate; NOCHOL 2023 no benefit

q: Which statement about systemic therapy for penile cancer is FALSE?
o: Cisplatin-based neoadjuvant therapy suits N+ disease
Surgery after progression on chemo is futile
Bleomycin regimens are preferred first line
e: Bleomycin gave no better responses than cisplatin and caused fatal lung toxicity: discouraged. Neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy (e.g., TIP) for node-positive disease can enable curative resection; consolidation surgery for responders; not for progressors (rapid death). Adjuvant chemotherapy for >2 nodes, ENE or pelvic nodes (VBM 82% vs 37% 5-year survival in one centre). PLND for >1 positive inguinal node or ENE. InPACT is testing multimodal therapy; palliative RT helps. No level 1 evidence defines the best strategy.

q: Which statement about distal renal tubular acidosis (dRTA) is FALSE?
o: Sodium alkali is preferred long term
e: Sodium alkali can promote calcium stones (especially pH >7); potassium citrate is preferred. dRTA: inability to lower urine pH below 5.3; incomplete form stays in acid-base balance. Acidosis mobilises bone calcium and impairs tubular reabsorption, causing hypercalciuria and low bone density; hypocitraturia. As stone phosphate content rises (CaOx → apatite), RTA rises from 5% to 39% and hyperparathyroidism from 2% to 10%.
s: Ch 92 Stone evaluation and medical management
b: Potassium citrate preferred to sodium alkali

q: Which statement about non-SCC penile tumours is FALSE?
o: Priapism is the commonest sign of metastasis
Penile lymphoma requires a systemic search
Epidemic Kaposi sarcoma is linked to HHV-8
e: Buschke-Löwenstein (giant condyloma) destroys tissue by compression but does not metastasise; excise completely; malignant change has been shown. Imiquimod is the standard topical treatment for condyloma. Kaposi sarcoma: HHV-8. Penile metastases: priapism, swelling, nodules; usually from an obvious primary; poor prognosis. Penile lymphoma: look for systemic disease. Melanoma and basal cell carcinoma are rare (sun-protected skin); BCC is curable; melanoma curable early (immunotherapy for advanced). Sarcomas recur locally, rarely metastasise. Extramammary Paget: intraepidermal spread, wide local excision.

q: In children with chronic kidney disease, anaemia is mainly due to:
e: Renal erythropoietin falls and urea suppresses red cell production. Book distractors corrected: CKD under 6 years is mostly congenital (CAKUT), not acquired IgA nephropathy; uraemic platelet dysfunction increases bleeding (not thrombosis); cardiac function is often abnormal; electrolyte disturbance (e.g., hyperkalaemia) risks arrhythmia.

q: Which penile primary carries little or no risk of nodal metastasis?
e: Carcinoma in situ and verrucous carcinoma carry little or no metastatic risk, so groin staging is not needed for them.

q: In penile cancer, pelvic lymph node dissection is recommended when:
o: The primary is T2 with a negative groin
The patient is obese with impalpable nodes
e: PLND for >1 positive inguinal node or extranodal extension; pelvic nodes are second-echelon.

q: After ilioinguinal lymphadenectomy, adjuvant chemotherapy is NOT routinely needed for:
o: More than two positive inguinal nodes
e: Consider adjuvant chemotherapy for >2 nodes, ENE or pelvic nodes; VBM gave 82% vs 37% 5-year survival in one centre (bleomycin is now discouraged).

q: Primary radiotherapy for penile cancer suits:
o: Young man, 3 cm superficial glans lesion
An elderly man with a 6 cm invasive tumour
A man with deep cavernosal invasion
e: RT suits small (2–4 cm) superficial exophytic glans/coronal lesions in young men, those refusing surgery, and palliation of metastases.

q: In uric acid stone disease, allopurinol is mainly indicated when urinary uric acid exceeds:
e: Alkalinisation is the key; allopurinol (xanthine oxidase inhibitor) mainly for marked hyperuricosuria; fluids lower concentration; thiazides and calcium restriction have no role.
s: Ch 92 Stone evaluation and medical management
b: Use if urinary uric acid >1500 mg/day

q: After Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, the key metabolic stone risk is:
e: Bypass: hyperoxaluria, low volume, hypocitraturia. Band or sleeve: mainly low volume.
s: Ch 92 Stone evaluation and medical management

q: Long-term acetohydroxamic acid therapy can cause:
e: AHA 250 mg tds inhibits urease, preventing new struvite stones and growth; minor side effects in up to 30% (headache, nausea, anaemia, rash, alopecia).
s: Ch 92 Stone evaluation and medical management

q: The commonest malignancy in a female urethral diverticulum is:
e: Adenocarcinoma predominates in urethral diverticula, unlike bladder diverticula, where urothelial carcinoma is commonest.

q: Megacalycosis is best described as:
e: Calyces dilated, malformed, sometimes increased in number; pelvis and UPJ normal; male 6:1; bilateral almost only in males, segmental unilateral only in females.

q: For pN+ disease after radical prostatectomy, the book suggests the best outcomes come from:
e: ECOG 3886 (Messing): immediate ADT improved survival over delayed; newer data suggest ADT plus RT is better still; no proven role for adjuvant chemotherapy or immunotherapy.
